author: @dulseteunji
text:
@@coffeebeanyup because Korean is a gender neutral language. There’re 그 and 그녀 which are gender specific, but these’re for translating Western pronouns that general Koreans don’t use them. If you use 그 and 그녀 for daily Korean speech or conversation, the listeners would feel awkward and alien as it doesn’t sound Korean and natural.

Korean distinguishes distance like “this” and “that” for personal pronouns which follow Korean three branches of 이, 그, and 저, and politeness or honorifics instead: 얘, 걔, 쟤, 이분, 그분, 저분.
